search_space: Exhaustive sweep for F=GF(3), A={0,1}, and GF(9)=GF(3)[t]/(t^2+1): all 6 elements ξ in GF(9)\Q(A), all 8 ordered triples in A^3, all 48 nonzero-quadruple checks for each map, and all 168 distinct-triple pair comparisons for each of the point and plane maps.
witness_description: In F=GF(3), take A={0,1} and ξ=t in GF(9)=GF(3)[t]/(t^2+1). The distinct triples (0,0,0) and (1,1,1) give point quadruples (0:t:t:t) and (0:1+t:1+t:1+t), and plane quadruples (t:−t:0:t) and (1+t:−(1+t):0:1+t).
refutation_explanation: Here Q(A)=GF(3), so t∉Q(A), and |A|^3=8≤9=3^2, equivalently |A|≤3^(2/3). Multiplication by the nonzero scalar (1+t)/t=1+2t sends each quadruple for (0,0,0) to the corresponding quadruple for (1,1,1). Thus both projective maps identify two distinct triples and are not injective.
